source_text:
Πάντες τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ἀκολουθεῖτε, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρί, καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς τοῖς ἀποστόλοις. τοὺς δὲ διακόνους ἐντρέπεσθε ὡς θεοῦ ἐντολήν. μηδεὶς χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου τι πρασσέτω τῶν ἀνηκόντων εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν. ἐκείνη βεβαία εὐχαριστία ἡγείσθω, ἡ ὑπὸ ἐπίσκοπον οὖσα ἢ ᾧ ἄν αὐτὸς ἐπιτρέψῃ.
ὅπου ἂν φανῇ ὁ ἐπίσκοπος, ἐκεῖ τὸ πλῆθος ἤτω, ὥσπερ ὅπου ἂν ᾖ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ἐκεῖ ἡ καθολικὴ ἐκκλησία. οὐκ ἐξόν ἐστιν χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου οὔτε βαπτίζειν οὔτε ἀγάπην ποιεῖν: ἀλλ’ ὃ ἂν ἐκεῖνος δοκιμάσῃ, τοῦτο καὶ τῷ θεῷ εὐάρεστον, ἵνα ἀσφαλὲς ᾖ καὶ βέβαιον πᾶν ὃ πράσσετε.
thought_title: Follow the bishop as Christ follows the Father
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, urging them to do nothing apart from the bishop and to regard only the Eucharist celebrated under the bishop's authority as valid.
pass_a_gloss: All of you follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ followed the Father, and follow the council of elders as the apostles. And respect the deacons as the command of God. Let no one do anything that pertains to the church apart from the bishop. Let that Eucharist be considered valid, the one that is under the bishop or the one to whom he himself may entrust it. Wherever the bishop may appear, there let the congregation be, just as wherever Jesus Christ may be, there is the catholic church. It is not permitted apart from the bishop either to baptize or to hold a love-feast; but whatever that one may approve, this is also pleasing to God, so that everything you do may be secure and valid.

choices.why: The verb means to follow or accompany; rendering it as 'follow' preserves the parallel structure with Christ following the Father.
The verb carries the sense of reverent regard or deference, fitting the command to honor deacons as God's command.
The adjective βέβαιος means firm, secure, or valid; 'valid' captures the legal-cultic force of what counts as a legitimate Eucharist.
In Ignatius's usage πλῆθος refers to the gathered church body; 'congregation' is more concrete than 'multitude' and fits the ecclesial context.
The phrase refers to the communal meal of the early church, distinct from the Eucharist; 'love-feast' is the standard English term for the agape meal.
This is the earliest attested use of the phrase; rendering it as 'catholic church' preserves the technical term rather than paraphrasing.

pass_b_english: All of you follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ followed the Father, and follow the council of elders as you would the apostles. Respect the deacons as God's command. Let no one do anything that pertains to the church without the bishop. Let that Eucharist be considered valid which is under the bishop or under someone he has entrusted.

Wherever the bishop appears, there let the congregation be, just as wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the whole church. It is not permitted to baptize or to hold a love-feast without the bishop. But whatever he approves, this is also pleasing to God, so that everything you do may be secure and valid.

last_rejected.quote: Respect the deacons as God's command
last_rejected.source_quote: τοὺς δὲ διακόνους ἐντρέπεσθε ὡς θεοῦ ἐντολήν
last_rejected.why: ἐντρέπεσθε means 'be subject to/reverence' not merely 'respect'; more critically, 'as God's command' treats ἐντολήν as object, but syntax is 'as [being] God's command' or 'as the command of God'—the deacons are to be revered as the command of God itself.
last_rejected.fix: Revere the deacons as the command of God
last_rejected.ruling: ἐντρέπεσθε = 'respect/reverence'; ὡς θεοῦ ἐντολήν = 'as God's command'—standard rendering, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: ἐπιτρέψῃ means 'to whom he entrusts/gives permission,' not 'someone he has entrusted' as a permanent deputy. The sense is 'to whom he gives permission' for that occasion.
last_rejected.fix: or to whom he gives permission
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπιτρέψῃ = 'entrusts/permits'; 'someone he has entrusted' is within normal range, no meaning changed.

last_rejected.why: φανῇ is subjunctive 'may appear/be found,' not 'appears' as if visible manifestation. 'Appears' suggests epiphany; 'is found' or 'may be' captures the contingent sense better.
last_rejected.fix: Wherever the bishop may be found
last_rejected.ruling: φανῇ with ἄν = 'appears/is found'; 'appears' is standard rendering, no misleading epiphany sense forced.

polish.changed: Clarified 'catholic church' as 'the whole church' to avoid later denominational meaning, and kept the council of elders term consistent.

notes.why: 'Council of elders' is the standard term, but two sections use different phrases for what appears to be the same body, which could confuse a reader about whether these are different groups.
notes.fix: Note that 'council of the apostles' and 'council of God' are metaphorical comparisons, not alternative names for the elders.

notes.why: First occurrence of 'catholic' in Christian literature; a modern reader may import later denominational meaning.
notes.fix: Note that 'catholic' here means 'universal,' not a later denomination.

polish.changed: Clarified that the council of elders is the same office as the presbyters, and explained the love-feast as the agape meal.

notes.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may miss the equivalence.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders (presbyters)' at first occurrence.
Gloss as the agape meal, a Christian fellowship meal.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may miss the equivalence.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders (presbyters)' at first occurrence.
